subject: Latency spike: NimbusHealth production — triage + customer update
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@nimbushealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production slowdown — spikes in text-generation latency

Hi Jonas / Laura,

We started seeing 95th/99th percentile latency spike on the inference endpoints for our production model at ~08:30 PDT. Average latency doubled and a subset of requests are timing out (~504) when we hit concurrent user flows. This is impacting patient-facing flows (consent forms).

Attached are two quick HAR captures from the web client and one API response sample. Can the Redwood team confirm whether this is a model-side problem or routing/backpressure? We are pausing a scheduled experiment but need an estimate for recovery time.

Thanks,
Sasha
Sasha Patel
Head of Integrations, Nimbus Health
[support ticket: NH-1187]
[attachment: nh-har-08-14.har (HAR)]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production slowdown — spikes in text-generation latency

Folks — forwarding Nimbus Health's report. Laura, please lead customer comms. Dylan/Marissa/Sean: triage and confirm root cause and mitigation options; we need a short-term mitigation and a roadmap ask if this is systemic.

Immediate asks:
- Dylan: can you share first-pass telemetry (GPU utilization, queue depth, per-shard latency) in 15m?
- Marissa: what operational levers do we have (burst routing, scale, eviction of small models)?
- Sean: if this is model-related, what product changes should we prioritize (e.g., kv-cache prewarm, batching heuristics)?
- Priyom: please prep a one-line partner-facing statement in case Nimbus escalates.

Attachments: I captured the trace link and a short HAR from the customer here.
[link: https://console.redwood.ai/trace/xyz-20260814]
[attachment: prod-trace-20260814.txt]
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production slowdown — spikes in text-generation latency

Quick triage notes (15m):
- Observed: sudden increase in per-request tokenization time + a burst of requests from one customer namespace at 08:28–08:35 PDT.
- Infra: GPU utilization on the affected pool rose to 95%, NVLink saturation on node 7; queue depth spiked causing increased tail latency. No OOMs.
- Traces: KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~88% to ~42% during the burst (see attached snapshot).

Short-term mitigations (can execute now):
1) Route Nimbus traffic to an alternate pool with spare capacity (will add ~40–60ms additional network hop but reduces tail). Estimated 7–10m to move.
2) Enable aggressive prefix-KV prewarm for Nimbus's common prompts (quick config change; 3–5m).
3) Apply transient QPS throttle for the namespace (config flag) to prevent queue buildup while we scale up; need product approval.

I can run 1+2 immediately if we agree. Longer-term, we need: improved cache warming on cold-start model variants and smarter admission control.

Attaching: prefix-cache-snapshot.json (excerpt), per-node-utilization.csv (trimmed).
[attachment: prefix-cache-snapshot.json]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production slowdown — spikes in text-generation latency

I support Dylan's plan. Operational notes:
- Routing to alternate pool: ops can cutover + health-check in ~8m; requires a quick ACL update (I’ll do it).
- Prefix prewarm: safe; minimal risk.
- QPS throttle: we need product sign-off because it affects SLA and billing. If product approves, I can set a conservative throttle that gives breathing room and auto-relaxes after 5m.

Risk: if we throttle too aggressively the customer flow breaks. Proposed immediate action: do (1) and (2) now, hold on (3) until we get sign-off from Sean/Jonas. I will coordinate the cutover and post a runbook entry.

Marissa
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Customer update: reported latency spike (NH-1187)

Hi Sasha — thanks for the report and the HARs. Quick update from the team:
- We identified a burst of traffic that caused cache degradation and GPU queueing; team is executing a two-step mitigation (routing + cache warm).
- Expected user impact: intermittent timeouts for a small percentage of requests; we expect visible improvement in 10–15 minutes.

Action items for you:
- If you can share the top-3 endpoints / prompt templates that saw the most traffic, we’ll prewarm those first.
- We will follow up with a short RCA and any product-level fixes if needed.

We appreciate the quick notice — I’ll confirm when the cutover completes.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed-rollout-plan.pdf]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production slowdown — spikes in text-generation latency

Hi Sasha — following up with the final status and next steps.

Summary / timeline:
- 08:40 PDT: ops routed your namespace to an alternate pool and enabled aggressive prefix prewarm.
- 08:50 PDT: noticeable reduction in 95th/99th p99 latency; timeouts fell to near-zero.
- We left the temporary routing in place for 1 hour to validate stability, then returned traffic to normal with cache warm persisted.

What we changed (short-term):
- Temporary pool routing to mitigate instantaneous load spikes.
- Aggressive prefix KV prewarm for the top 3 prompt templates (we used the HAR to pick these).

Next steps (roadmap asks / product):
- Product will prioritize a small project to improve automatic cache prewarming and a smarter admission controller for high-burst namespaces (owner: Sean; requested timeline: Q4).
- Ops will add an automated detection rule for KV hit-rate drops per-namespace and a playbook that suggests routing + prewarm.

Requested from Nimbus: please share the three most common prompt templates you used during the window (creds/PII redacted). That will let us ensure persistent warm caches and avoid repeated cutovers.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 20m postmortem with product + engineering to review the RCA and timeline for the product fix.

Thanks again for the quick escalation.

Jonas Weber
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
[jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198]
